rules.title: Algorithmic rent price fixing prohibited for Hoboken residential landlords
rules.requirement: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit in Hoboken may not engage in price fixing using algorithmic pricing. That means using software, algorithms, or data-sharing platforms to collect and analyze nonpublic competitor information from other real estate lessors in order to coordinate, recommend, or implement rental prices, lease terms, or occupancy levels among competing lessors. Nonpublic competitor information includes prices, supply levels, security deposits, ideal occupancy levels, lease termination and renewal dates, or other material terms that are less than 365 days old and not widely and readily available to the public at no cost.
rules.quoted_span: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing.
rules.exemptions: A residential dwelling unit is defined as a primary residence, excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities. This exclusion is not fully representable in the coverage predicate. Review it manually.
rules.interaction: Enforcement may be brought by the Division of Housing or an aggrieved private citizen in Hoboken Municipal Court. Penalties on conviction include one or more of the following: penalties under N.J.S.A. 40:49-5, a fine up to $2,000, or community service up to 90 days. Any interaction with state law is not addressed in this chunk.
